title.value: Effects of eight neuropsychiatric copy number variants on human brain structure
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the article, specifying the study's focus on the effects of eight neuropsychiatric copy number variants on human brain structure.
title.quote: Effects of eight neuropsychiatric copy number variants on human brain structure

analysis.description: The paper investigates the impact of eight different neuropsychiatric copy number variants (CNVs) on human brain structure using neuroimaging data. It employs multiple methodologies such as principal component analysis and multi-view pattern learning to identify distinct and shared effects of CNVs on brain morphometry.

type.justification: The study performs analyses on actual T1-weighted MRI data from CNV carriers and controls, making it empirical.
type.quote: We analyzed T1-weighted MRI data from clinically and non-clinically ascertained CNV carriers (deletion/duplication)... as well as 1296 non-carriers (controls).

name.justification: The paper focuses on brain structure and neuroimaging, which are key domains within neuroscience.
name.quote: we aimed to characterize and quantify the distinct brain morphometry effects and latent dimensions across 8 neuropsychiatric CNVs.

name.justification: The study involves T1-weighted MRI data analysis to understand brain structure changes due to CNVs, which falls under neuroimaging.
name.quote: Neuroimaging studies have only been performed for a few CNVs. Robust effects on total and regional brain volumes, cortical thickness (CT) and surface area (SA)...

name.justification: PCA is explicitly mentioned as a method used to quantify the shared variation of brain morphometry associated with eight CNVs.
name.quote: PCs were derived to quantify shared morphometry variation across CNVs.

is_contributed.justification: PCA is a well-established statistical method and not a contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: PCs were derived to quantify shared morphometry variation across CNVs.

is_executed.justification: PCA was actively used in the analysis within the scope of the paper.
is_executed.quote: PCs were derived to quantify shared morphometry variation across CNVs.

is_compared.justification: PCA results are compared to other methods like CCA in explaining brain morphometry variation.
is_compared.quote: A multivariate approach (PCA) quantified distinct and shared alterations across subsets of CNVs.

referenced_paper_title.value: Finding the needle in high-dimensional haystack: a tutorial on canonical correlation analysis.
referenced_paper_title.justification: PCA is a standard method and might not necessitate a specific reference, but referencing CCA tutorials indicates comparison of methods.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Wang H-T, et al. Finding the needle in high-dimensional haystack: a tutorial on canonical correlation analysis.

name.justification: CCA is described as a pattern-learning algorithm used for the joint analysis of genetic and morphometry brain data.
name.quote: a multi-view pattern-learning algorithm was carried out for the joint analysis of genetic and morphometry brain data, to identify latent ‘gene-morphometry dimensions’ (canonical correlation analysis, CCA).

is_contributed.justification: CCA is a well-established analysis method and not a new contribution of this paper.

is_compared.justification: CCA results are discussed and compared with PCA for validating shared genetic-morphometry dimensions.
is_compared.quote: A second multivariate approach (CCA), jointly analyzing genetic and morphometry data, confirmed the latent CNV-brain dimensions identified by PCA.
